title: k8s-node-provisioning-incident-scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Intermittent node provisioning failures in EKS fleet for staging cluster (staging-us-west-2). New spot-backed nodes frequently stuck in 'NotReady' or fail to join after cloud-init.
- Symptoms observed since 2025-11-18; spike after autoscaler bump on 2025-11-19.
- Impact: CI runners scheduled to staging node pool failing ~30% of runs.

What I saw (timeline):
- 2025-11-18 09:12 - first alerts: kube-scheduler backlog, pods Pending with events: "0/3 nodes are available: 3 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate."
- 2025-11-19 03:45 - autoscaler added 6 spot instances, several never transitioned to Ready.
- 2025-11-20 14:10 - manual repro on a failed host; SSH'd in and collected logs.

Commands tried (notes + outputs trimmed):
- aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids i-0abcd1234 -> instance shows running, security groups OK, subnet same as working nodes

- ssh ec2-user@ip-10-0-5-23.us-west-2.compute.internal
  - journalctl -u cloud-init -b --no-pager | tail -n 80\    -> saw cloud-init finished but late: 'Failed to run listener: timed out' messages earlier
  - sudo journalctl -u kubelet -b -n 200 --no-pager\    -> kubelet repeatedly: E1103 14:05:12 kubelet_node_status.go:97] Error getting node status: network plugin not ready: cni config uninitialized
  - sudo cat /var/log/cloud-init-output.log\    -> small errors about docker.service failing to start (cgroup v2 mismatch)

- kubectl get nodes -o wide\  
  NAME                       STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION   INTERNAL-IP   EXTERNAL-IP   OS-IMAGE             KERNEL-VERSION
  ip-10-0-5-23.ec2.internal  NotReady   <none>   10m   v1.25.8   10.0.5.23     <none>        Amazon Linux 2       5.10.0-21

- kubectl describe node ip-10-0-5-23.ec2.internal\  
  Conditions:
    Ready    False   KubeletNotReady  kubelet is not ready: NetworkPluginNotReady: cni config uninitialized
  Taints:
    node.kubernetes.io/unreachable:NoSchedule for 8m
  Events:
    Normal  NodeHasSufficientMemory   8m   kubelet, ip-10-0-5-23  Node had enough resource: memory
    Warning NodeNotReady             7m   kubelet, ip-10-0-5-23  Node became NotReady

- ls /etc/cni/net.d/  -> directory empty on failing nodes; working nodes have 10-calico.conflist
- systemctl status kubelet\  -> active (running) but logs show repeated "cni config uninitialized"
- crictl ps -a --runtime-endpoint unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock\  -> containerd running, but runtime fails to create pod infra container with error: "failed to setup network for sandbox: NetworkPlugin cni failed to set up pod netns"

Helm/cluster config checks:
- Helm release: calico configured as daemonset. helm get values calico -n kube-system shows values mostly default, IP autodetection uses AWS metadata.
- kubectl -n kube-system get daemonset calico-node -o wide shows pods crashlooping on new nodes? On working nodes calico-node is Running. On failing nodes calico-node stuck Pending (no CNI dir).

Hypotheses so far:
1) cloud-init / userdata ordering race - kubelet starts before CNI plugin is installed/started (calico). New AMI change extended boot time so CNI daemonset didn't run before kubelet registered.
   - Evidence: empty /etc/cni/net.d and kubelet logs show network plugin uninitialized.
   - Repro: join a node but delay kubelet start until CNI files present -> see node become Ready.
2) AMI change introduced cgroup v2 vs v1 mismatch causing container runtime not to start properly, preventing CNI pod from running (calico depends on container runtime).
   - Evidence: cloud-init logs showing docker.service failing and cgroup message in cloud-init-output.log. But our fleet uses containerd; some nodes show docker remnants.
3) IAM role / node bootstrap permission regression preventing kubelet from pulling images for calico or writing to /etc/cni.
   - Evidence: image pull errors in calico pod events? (haven't seen consistently)

Quick experiments run from host (manual):
- sudo systemctl stop kubelet; create /etc/cni/net.d/10-fake.conflist with minimal bridge config; start kubelet -> node becomes Ready (for test pods).\  -> This strongly suggests race between kubelet and CNI provisioning rather than IAM.
- sudo systemctl restart containerd && sudo journalctl -u containerd -n 200 shows containerd healthy on test node after restart, calico pod then scheduled and created CNI files.

Actions taken (so far):
- Rolled out a temporary init script in ASG userdata to mkdir /etc/cni/net.d and touch a placeholder file before kubelet systemd unit is enabled.
- Added preStop hook to autoscaler to drain older nodes before scale-up to reduce churn (WIP).
- Opened JIRA-INC-1123 and assigned to infra on-call; linked PR to infra repo with userdata change (PR-432).

Open questions / next steps:
- Need to confirm whether AMI update is root cause (we changed base image on 2025-11-15). Compare cloud-init logs between last-known-good AMI and new AMI.
- Can we change kubelet systemd unit to start after cloud-init finishes? Potential fix: add After=cloud-final.service and add ConditionPathExists=/etc/cni/net.d in kubelet.service drop-in. Evaluate if safe.
- Investigate container runtime differences: are some nodes using docker/legacy remnants? Standardize on containerd.
- Add lifecycle hook in ASG to wait for calico daemonset readiness before marking instance healthy in ELB/target group.

Notes / commands to reproduce locally (dev box):
1) spin up an instance with same AMI + userdata from ASG
2) replicate: systemctl start kubelet early -> see NotReady and missing CNI
3) create placeholder /etc/cni/net.d file and restart kubelet -> becomes Ready

Temporary mitigation for staging cluster (applied 2025-11-21):
- userdata placeholder + systemctl disable kubelet until cloud-init finishes (see PR-432) rolled to staging ASG; monitoring shows Ready rate improved from 68% -> 92% for new nodes over 24h.

Longer-term fixes to consider:
- Bake AMI with CNI binaries and config preinstalled and tested (preferred).
- Add start ordering to kubelet service or use cloud-init to defer kubelet enablement until CNI files created.
- Add ASG lifecycle hook / Lambda that waits on calico daemonset readiness before completing instance lifecycle.

Misc logs / error snippets (copied raw):
- kubelet: "E1103 14:05:12.123456   1234 kubelet_node_status.go:97] Error getting node status: network plugin not ready: cni config uninitialized"
- calico-node pod event: "Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to setup network for sandbox \"...\": NetworkPlugin cni failed to set up pod netns: open /etc/cni/net.d/10-calico.conflist: no such file or directory"
- cloud-init: "WARNING:cloudinit:Not writing config - file exists /run/config/instance-data.txt" followed by "ERROR:cloud-init:Failed to run cloud-init modules: timed out" (timing suspicious)

TODO (short):
- [ ] Compare AMI cloud-init logs between good/bad images (assign to Alex)
- [ ] Add kubelet systemd drop-in to defer start (POC)
- [ ] Bake CNI into AMI and test across AZs (infra project)
- [ ] Add automated check in ASG lifecycle to wait for daemonset pods to be Running before marking healthy
- [ ] Add more metrics: node provisioning time, time to first CNI file, calico pod start delay

If you pick this up: start with the two experiments I ran (placeholder CNI file + delayed kubelet start) and reproduce on a fresh instance. Notes in PR-432 include the exact userdata snippet I used.

End of scratchpad.
